title: Execution Inspection Proxy — Experimentation & Rollout Runbook
author: Jordan Li
content:
Overview

This page defines the Execution Inspection Proxy (EIP): a lightweight, in-path inspection layer designed to enable low-overhead sampling, causal tracing, and feature experimentation against live inference traffic. The intent is to provide a safe way to surface execution-level signals (kernel selection, batching decisions, KV-cache warmup, and tail latency contributors) without modifying the core runtime or blocking production flows.

Goals and non-goals
- Goals:
  - Capture causal telemetry for sampled requests: kernel selection, batch composition, queue wait, dispatch, and kernel execution durations.
  - Support non-invasive shadow sampling and replay capture for downstream profiling.
  - Provide a controlled canary rollout pattern with clear safety gates and rollback criteria.
  - Emit structured events compatible with our observability pipeline (OTLP/jaeger-compatible spans + JSON payloads to kinesis).
- Non-goals:
  - This proxy is not a replacement for full kernel-level instrumentation. It intentionally samples and reconstructs rather than tracing every token event.

Architectural overview
- Deployment: the EIP runs as a co-located process on runtime nodes (container sidecar or host process) and accepts a mirrored subset of requests via the request-router. It has two logical components: the fast-path forwarder and the asynchronous inspector.
- Fast-path forwarder:
  - For mirrored/inspected requests, forward to runtime with TCP passthrough and minimal packetization to preserve latency characteristics.
  - Add only a single hop and a configurable metadata header (x-eip-sampled: id, sample-rate, sample-reason).
- Asynchronous inspector:
  - Receives sampling copies via the forwarder and enriches them by collecting decision traces from scheduler hooks and kernel handshake messages.
  - Persists captures to the profiling bucket and emits telemetry events.

Textual diagram
  Request Router --> [Runtime Node] --> (EIP forwarder) --> Runtime Core
                                     
                                     (copied sample) --> (EIP inspector) --> telemetry / profiling-bucket

Kernel scheduling interactions and safety considerations
- Priority propagation:
  1) The EIP must not change runtime scheduling priorities. To avoid priority inversion, the proxy only annotates metadata; it never adjusts request priority headers unless explicitly enabled in experiment mode.
  2) When experiment mode is enabled, a separate gating service (priority-gate) authorizes transient priority hints stored in a short-lived config (TTL 60s) to the scheduler.
- Backpressure and admission control:
  - EIP respects runtime admission controller signals. If the runtime returns HTTP 429 for a mirrored request, inspector drops additional enrichment traffic for that request to avoid amplification.
- Kernel handshake correlation:
  - The inspector consumes the kernel handshake stream (read-only subscription) to correlate kernel ID -> execution timings. This subscription path is throttled to 1% of live handshakes by default.

Profiling & benchmarking plan
- Success metrics for experiment:
  - End-to-end p50 overhead introduced by EIP on observed requests <= 0.5ms.
  - End-to-end p99 overhead <= 5ms and never larger than 5% relative increase over baseline p99.
  - CPU usage for EIP sidecar <= 3% of node CPU under typical traffic; memory overhead < 200MB.
  - Sampling fidelity: inspector correlates >= 95% of sampled requests to kernel handshake when sampling rate is 1/1000.
- Benchmarks to run:
  1) Baseline synthetic workload: 10k RPS mixed seq-lengths (8/64/512) using shadow-generator v2. Command: 
     ./shadow-generator --rps 10000 --mix "0.6:8,0.3:64,0.1:512" --duration 30m --dest <router>
  2) Canary real-traffic mirror: 0.1% live traffic mirrored for 24 hours with continuous telemetry checks.
  3) Load spike stress test: inject a 5x traffic spike for 10 minutes and observe EIP behavior under kernel negotiation churn.
- Measurement guidance:
  - Use histogram exports for latency (client-observed), EIP forwarder add-on latency, and inspector processing time.
  - Collect kernel handshake correlation rate and amount of additional memory allocated for captured artifacts.
  - Compare generation token throughput and tail latency against baseline snapshots collected immediately prior to EIP enablement.

Runbook: Canary rollout (step-by-step)
1) Pre-checks (owner: runtime-ops)
   - Confirm benchmark baseline snapshots exist (p50/p95/p99 for last 24h).
   - Ensure profiling-bucket has >= 5GB free and write policy enforces retention 30d.
   - Verify OTLP pipeline is green and downstream parsers accept EIP schema.
2) Deploy to 2% of fleet as sidecar in passive mode (sampling disabled, headers present) and run 2-hour smoke watch.
3) Enable sampling at 0.01% (1/10000) for 1 hour; run automated checks:
   - CPU delta per node < 2%
   - Additional p99 latency delta < 3%
   - No increase in kernel failure counts or eviction incidents
4) If automated checks pass, raise sample-rate to 0.1% and observe for 6 hours.
5) If still stable, raise to 1% for 24 hours and run the full profiling capture pipeline to produce sample artifacts for kernel team analysis.
6) If any safety gate fails, follow rollback procedure below.

Rollback procedure (critical)
- Trigger conditions (any):
  - Measured p99 latency increase > 5% absolute compared to baseline or > 10% relative increase.
  - Node-level CPU increase > 5% sustained for 10 minutes.
  - Any increase in error-rate or kernel OOM/invocations > threshold.
- Immediate steps:
  1) Toggle sampling to 0% via feature-flag (flag name: eip_sampling_rate) and set traffic routing to bypass EIP forwarder.
  2) If bypass fails, stop the EIP process using: systemctl stop eip-sidecar or kubectl delete pod <eip-pod> --namespace runtime-canary
  3) Open incident with runtime-sre and tag priority P1. Attach profiling artifacts.
  4) Follow post-incident diagnostics checklist (see Diagnostics section).

Diagnostics: investigation checklist
- Correlate any latency spike with:
  - Request-size mix changes in the router logs.
  - Kernel handshake error counts in the last 30 minutes.
  - Memory pressure events (dmesg/kernel logs) and GPU eviction traces.
- Useful queries (PromQL examples):
  - avg_over_time(eip_forwarder_latency_ms[5m]) by (node) > 1.0
  - rate(kernel_handshake_errors_total[5m]) > 0
  - sum(container_cpu_usage_seconds_total{pod=~"eip-sidecar.*"}) by (node)

Known issues and mitigations
- Issue: occasional handshake desynchronization during heavy evictions.
  - Symptom: inspector cannot correlate kernel ID to request and marks sample as orphaned.
  - Mitigation: enable conservative sampling (lower rate) during high eviction windows; implement a short buffer (250ms) in inspector to wait for delayed handshake.
- Issue: small spikes in p99 when inspector writes large captures to disk synchronously.
  - Mitigation: use async write workers with backpressure (queue size 512). Limit per-request artifact size to 128KB.
- Issue: increased observability pipeline cardinality when sampling rate becomes large.
  - Mitigation: normalize dimension tags (drop high-cardinality request-id tag in telemetry; reserve it only for artifact payloads).

Telemetry & dashboarding (owner: observability)
- Minimum signals to emit:
  - eip.forwarder.latency_ms (p50/p95/p99)
  - eip.inspector.processing_ms (histogram)
  - eip.sample.correlation_rate (ratio of inspector->handshake correlates)
  - eip.disk.write_backpressure_events
  - eip.node.cpu_pct and eip.node.mem_bytes
- Suggested dashboards:
  - EIP Health overview (per-cluster): latency trends, CPU/mem, correlation_rate, artifact write volume.
  - Canary gate panel: real-time pass/fail indicators for sampling checks.

Appendix: sample config (YAML)
```yaml
# eip-config.yaml
enabled: true
mode: canary # passive | canary | experiment
sampling_rate: 0.001 # fractional (0.001 = 0.1%)
max_artifact_size_bytes: 131072
artifact_write_workers: 4
handshake_subscribe_rate: 0.01 # throttle handshake subscription to 1% by default
forwarder_override_header: "x-eip-sampled"
backpressure_queue_size: 512
```

Appendix: quick CLI & debug commands
- Check status: kubectl -n runtime get pods -l app=eip-sidecar -o wide
- Tail logs (fast-path): kubectl -n runtime logs -f deployment/eip-forwarder
- Force disable sampling: curl -X POST $EIP_ADMIN/flags -d '{"eip_sampling_rate": 0}'
